messages:
acme_ops: hey team — started seeing a spike of 429s from our prod service hitting the dedicated pool after our plan migration this morning. traffic volume didn't change, latency is fine, but ~30% of requests are getting 429. sample request id: req_0a3f9. can someone triage?

olivia_support: sorry about that — can you confirm you're on a Dedicated pool and share the tenant id + a sample 429 response body/headers? we can triage quota vs pool-level throttling.

acme_ops: we're definitely on Dedicated (reserved pool: acme-reserved-1). tenant id: tenant-acme-77. here's a copied 429 we got: 

```json
{
  "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
  "message": "Quota exceeded: per-tenant rate units",
  "headers": {"x-rate-limit-remaining": "0", "x-rate-limit-reset": "161"}
}
```

olivia_support: thanks. pinging @raj_oncall to check the quota plumbing and pool autoscale behavior. also @deploy-bot shows a plan-migration job ran at 07:12 UTC for tenant-acme-77, could be related.

deploy-bot: plan-migration job job-id=pm-849 completed for tenant-acme-77 at 07:12 UTC.

raj_oncall: looking at the tenant quota record now. quick hypothesis: migration script applied rate units using an "hours" denom instead of "minutes" (we've seen this once before) which would effectively reduce rate capacity by 60x. pulling the DB record...

raj_oncall: db snippet for tenant-acme-77 quota: 

```yaml
tenant_id: tenant-acme-77
plan: growth-v2
rate_units: 1000
denom: hours
burst_units: 200
```

raj_oncall: if denom==hours that means 1000 units/hour -> ~16.6 units/minute. their app expects ~1000 units/minute. that matches the 429 spike after migration.

acme_ops: oh that would explain it. billing expected to move us to 60k units/hour (i.e., 1000/min) but if the denom flipped to hours on the stored record we'd lose capacity. can you confirm this is what the runtime is enforcing? any quick mitigation?

olivia_support: confirmed — runtime token-bucket logs show steady depletion of per-tenant tokens and immediate 429s. sample runtime log lines: 

```
[2026-03-17T07:25:12Z] tenant=tenant-acme-77 alloc=16 remain=0 -> 429 rate_limit_exceeded
[2026-03-17T07:25:45Z] tenant=tenant-acme-77 bucket_refill_ms=60000 refill_amount=16
```

olivia_support: mitigation options: 1) apply an emergency tenant-level override to restore expected units-per-minute, 2) rollback the migration mapping for that tenant, or 3) temp bump the Dedicated pool routing rule to bypass per-tenant enforcement (not ideal). i'll propose an override now.

raj_oncall: agree override is fastest. i can issue an override to set units_per_minute=1200 for tenant-acme-77 and set an audit tag so accounting can reconcile. doing it now.

raj_oncall: executed support-api call: 

```bash
curl -XPOST https://internal-api.support/v1/tenants/tenant-acme-77/overrides 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SVC_TOKEN" 
  -d '{"units_per_minute":1200, "reason":"hotfix: denom mismatch after plan-migration"}'
```

raj_oncall: override applied. please verify your requests now.

acme_ops: testing... good — 429s dropped to near-zero and tail latency is normal. huge thanks. what's the permanent fix?

olivia_support: permanent fix is twofold: A) update the migration script to write denom consistently (we'll change to canonical field units_per_minute during migration), and B) run a one-off audit for recent migrations where plan-migration job completed in the last 48 hours to catch any other tenants with hours/min mismatch. i'll create a support ticket and a follow-up with the migrations team.

emily_account: tagging from accounts — we'll need to reconcile billing since our contractual language assumed per-minute units. please add billing to the audit. set priority high if other tenants are affected.

raj_oncall: note on autoscale: Dedicated pool autoscaler didn't help here because the pool had available GPU capacity — this is strictly per-tenant logical throttling (token bucket). autoscale only affects infra capacity, not tenant quota enforcement. noisy neighbor not the cause in this case.

acme_ops: can you share repro steps so we can avoid hitting this again in staging?

olivia_support: repro checklist: 
1) confirm tenant plan in billing UI and note expected units/min. 
2) run `GET /internal/admin/tenants/{tenant_id}/quota` and confirm denom/field semantics. 
3) run a small load test at expected QPS and confirm `x-rate-limit-remaining` header stays >0 for 5m. 
4) if migrating multiple tenants, run a dry-run of migration script that prints the computed units_per_minute and fail on any denom mismatch. 

olivia_support: i'll open a ticket (SUP-7832) to onboard billing + migrations + infra. will schedule the audit and follow up in this thread.

acme_ops: appreciate the fast turnaround. please keep us posted and we can coordinate re-tests.

olivia_support: follow-up created and assigned. closing the hot-issue since override fixed production. leaving thread open for audit updates. :thumbsup:
